name: Oklahoma

law.name: Revised Uniform Athlete Agents Act (70 O.S. 820.1 and following, 2021)

covers_nil_agents: Yes. The act covers agents for endorsement deals, and 70 O.S. 820.24 sets rules for NIL representation agreements.
contract_warning: Warning to student athlete. If you sign this contract: 1. You may lose your eligibility to compete as a student athlete in your sport; 2. If you have an athletic director, within seventy-two (72) hours after signing this contract or before the next scheduled athletic event in which you participate, whichever occurs first, both you and your athlete agent must notify your athletic director that you have entered into this contract and provide the name and contact information of the athlete agent; and 3. You may cancel this contract within fourteen (14) days after signing it. Cancellation of this contract may not reinstate your eligibility as a student athlete in your sport.
summary: Register with the Secretary of State. $1,000, good for 2 years.

steps.text: Fill out the Application for Registration of Athlete Agent

steps.detail: Same fee if you're registered in another state.

steps.text: Mail it to the Secretary of State
Register with each school's compliance office, if it asks
steps.detail: Most schools have their own agent sign-up.

steps.text: Tell the athletic director in writing before you first contact the athlete
steps.detail: This also applies before you contact a minor's parent, or anyone you want to sway the athlete. If the athlete reached out first, tell the athletic director within 10 days.

steps.text: Use a written contract with all required items
steps.detail: Say you're registered in Oklahoma and list your other states. Add your pay and how it's figured, other pay you get for the deal, anyone else being paid, expenses, services, length and date signed.

steps.text: Put the warning to student athlete in bold in the contract
steps.detail: Use Oklahoma's set wording. If the athlete is a minor, change it to speak to the parent too.

steps.text: Have the athlete sign a separate eligibility warning
steps.detail: It says signing may cost them their eligibility. A parent or guardian signs it if the athlete is a minor.

steps.text: Have a parent or guardian sign the contract if the athlete is a minor
Give the athlete a copy of the contract and the warning when they sign
steps.detail: Give it to the parent if the athlete is a minor.

steps.text: Tell the athletic director in writing within 72 hours of signing
steps.detail: Or before the athlete's next game, whichever comes first. The athlete must tell them too. The athlete (or parent of a minor) may cancel within 14 days.

steps.text: Tell the new school within 72 hours if your athlete enrolls later
steps.detail: Count from when you knew or should have known they enrolled.

steps.text: Spell out duties and fees in every NIL deal you sign
steps.detail: The NIL agreement must be in writing and signed by both of you. Make sure the athlete tells their school about you.

steps.text: Date the contract the day it's signed
steps.detail: Oklahoma and federal law (SPARTA) ban backdating or postdating it.
Each client's name and address, each contract and what you spent to recruit each athlete. The Secretary of State may inspect them.

steps.text: Never mislead athletes or give them anything that could cost their eligibility
steps.detail: A gift is only OK if you tell the athletic director within 72 hours and the athlete signs a warning. Never contact athletes while unregistered.
Use the Secretary of State's renewal form and update all your info. The fee is set in 70 O.S. 820.9.

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. The House is out until Nov 9 and leaders say it won't pass as-is. It dies if not enacted by Jan 3, 2027.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap agent fees at 5% of an endorsement deal and limit contracts to the athlete's eligibility.
